answers.rationale: The ATL option preserves an evening setup attempt before the 8 p.m. cutoff while saving $146 versus the nonstop; clear weather, carry-on-style luggage, and no Friday teaching make the 58-minute connection proportionate. The late CLT option misses the useful setup window. History shows context-dependent choices between direct and connecting flights, not a fixed nonstop-first rule or fare threshold.

The nonstop arrives with enough time to reach the classroom and use the 5:30-7:00 p.m. check-in window without relying on a 44-minute connection or a nominal 5:55 p.m. airport arrival. The $135 premium buys directly relevant setup protection. Prior decisions support paying more when same-evening presenter or room access is at stake, but do not establish a blanket nonstop premium rule.

The 10:40 CLT itinerary arrives before the 4 p.m. packet deadline with a comfortable 90-minute connection and avoids the moderate evening snow risk. The early nonstop adds a large, unnecessary premium when there is no next-day teaching, while the 1:55 option misses packet pickup and reaches Pittsburgh during the higher-risk period. History reflects choosing connections when their timing is sufficient, rather than a fixed direct-flight preference.

The 10:55 departure reaches MSP around 2:05, leaving roughly 85 minutes before the 3:30 rehearsal and about 55 minutes after the stated airport-to-site transfer. With no Tuesday campus constraint and fares within $60, the 6:15 departure creates unnecessary idle time; later flights miss rehearsal. Prior departure choices vary with required arrival windows, so the record does not support a fixed early-flight or after-noon policy.
